sourcedFrom: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 (2020)
cleanIntro: A Gold Reserve strips in two movements like any break gun, and its one real difference from the Silver is what happens when you open it: the ejectors throw fired shells clear and leave live ones sitting elevated in the chamber. That is a good feature and a bad habit-former — the gun looks emptier than it is. Forearm latch, barrels off the hinge pins, and the whole strip is done.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward, fingers clear of the trigger
steps.action: Set the tang safety fully back to ON and keep the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless. On a double there are two live chambers and one trigger; nothing touches it until both are proven empty.
steps.quote: Set the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position. During unloading, never allow your fingers or any other object to contact the trigger.
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Top lever right, and help the barrels down
steps.action: Push the top lever fully to the right and assist the barrels open by pulling down on the forearm. Letting a double fall open under its own weight batters the hinge and the standing breech over time.
steps.quote: Open the action by moving the top lever fully to the right, and assist the barrel swing with your hand by pulling down on the forearm
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: ⛔ Ejectors THROW the fired shells — and only the fired ones
steps.action: Watch what the gun does as it opens. A Gold Reserve carries automatic selective ejectors: fired shells are thrown clear, unfired ones are merely lifted above the chamber for you to take out by hand. "Selective" is the word to hold on to — a live round will NOT be ejected, so a gun that threw one empty and nothing else may still have a loaded chamber under your thumb.
steps.aside: The ejectors are automatic selective ejectors which mean they eject only fired shotshells.
steps.quote: Fired shells will be ejected and unfired shells will be elevated above the chamber on Gold Reserve models with automatic selective ejectors.
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Both chambers and both barrels, looked at and felt
steps.action: Check the chambers and then look through both barrels. Two tubes means two chances to leave something behind, and a bore obstruction on a double is not survivable for the barrel.
steps.quote: After unloading always visually and physically inspect the chamber, and barrels to be certain all of the shotshells have been removed, and the firearm is completely unloaded!
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, p.16

steps.title: Re-prove it empty before a part moves
steps.action: Safety ON, action open, chamber and barrels checked again. The book asks for this a second time at the head of the strip and it is worth doing rather than assuming the last two minutes still hold.
steps.quote: Before disassembling the firearm, set the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position and keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction.
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — DISASSEMBLY, p.19

steps.title: Forearm off — LIFT the latch
steps.action: Lift the forearm latch and pull the forearm away from the barrels. ⛔ Lift, not push: this is the over/under's mechanism, and the side-by-side Reserve uses a push-button release instead. Working the wrong one is levering at a part that does not move.
steps.quote: To remove the forearm, lift the forearm latch and pull the forearm away from the barrels (Figure 10).
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — DISASSEMBLY, p.19

steps.title: Top lever right, barrels down and off the hinge pins
steps.action: Push the top lever fully right, pull the barrels down and then lift them to disengage the half-round cuts from the round hinge pins. Support the barrels with both hands as they come free — there is nothing holding them once the cuts clear.
steps.quote: Move the top lever fully to the right, and assist the barrel swing with your hand by pulling down the barrels and lifting up to disengage the barrels from the round hinge pins in the stock/receiver assembly
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — DISASSEMBLY, p.19

steps.title: Field strip complete — three pieces
steps.action: Barrels, forearm, stock and receiver. That is the whole strip and Mossberg's line for it; nothing else comes apart for cleaning.
steps.cite: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Part No. 104723, typeset 09/09/20 — DISASSEMBLY, p.19

deepAbsentReason: The Reserve O/U book publishes one teardown and stops at barrels-off; further disassembly is assigned to a qualified gunsmith or the Product Service Center in its own words. ⛔ No deeper path is invented for it.

cleaning.name: STRIP FIRST, AND CLEAR THE BENCH OF AMMUNITION
tasks: Take it apart before cleaning, not after
No shells anywhere near the solvent
Safety ON and both chambers re-checked
Eye protection through cleaning AND assembly
cleaning.quote: Always make sure that no ammunition is located in the area where you clean your firearm.
cleaning.src: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.20

cleaning.name: BOTH BORES AND BOTH CHAMBERS
tasks: Solvent and brush through each barrel separately
Patches until clean, then one lightly oiled patch
Chokes out, threads wiped, before the barrels go away
Check both bores are clear of patches before reassembly
cleaning.quote: To clean and lubricate your firearm, first disassemble it (refer to the Disassembly section of this owner’s manual).
cleaning.src: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.20

cleaning.name: HINGE, LUGS AND STANDING BREECH
tasks: Wipe the hinge pins and the half-round cuts in the barrel lug
Clean the standing breech face and the extractor or ejector seats
A trace of grease on the hinge pins, oil everywhere else
Do not flood the head of the stock — oil softens the wood
cleaning.quote: Wear eye protection during cleaning and assembly to protect your eyes from oil splatter and spring loaded components.
cleaning.src: RESERVE™ SERIES OVER/UNDER BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, p.20

reassembly: Safety ON. Barrels and receiver both wiped dry of surplus oil.
Half-round cuts in the barrel lug onto the receiver's round hinge pins.
Top lever fully right, swing the barrels closed, release the lever and let it centre itself.
Forearm plate to the receiver, forearm swung up against the barrels, latch down.
Open and close it a few times to feel the barrels move freely.
Function test before it is put away.
fncheck: Prove both chambers empty, safety fully rearward to ON. Open and close the gun several times — the barrels should swing freely and the top lever should return to centre each time. Closed, safety ON, pull the trigger: no hammer fall. Finger off, safety forward to FIRE: still no fall on its own. Then the trigger should drop it. ⛔ If the top lever does not return to centre when the gun closes, the bolt is not fully engaging the lump and the gun must not be fired.
